question: Can one optimizer framework combine recursive variance reduction with Adam-, Lion-, and Shampoo-style preconditioning to reduce the token and wall-clock cost of language-model training?

key_findings.claim: MARS unifies multiple adaptive optimizers by applying a scaled STORM-like correction before a configurable preconditioner.
key_findings.evidence: The corrected gradient uses current and previous-parameter gradients on the same sample, is clipped, and then feeds AdamW-, Lion-, or Shampoo-like state updates; the paper derives Adan and Muon connections as special or approximate cases.

key_findings.claim: On the reported GPT-2 runs, MARS reaches a fixed validation loss with substantially fewer tokens than AdamW.
key_findings.evidence: For the 770M model, AdamW requires about 50B tokens to reach validation loss 2.58 while MARS reaches it near 28B; final reported losses are 2.511 for MARS-AdamW and 2.534 for MARS-Lion versus 2.568 for AdamW.

key_findings.claim: The inexpensive adjacent-minibatch approximation is the practical algorithm, but its theoretical link to the exact estimator remains empirical.
key_findings.evidence: Exact MARS needs two gradient evaluations on the same sample; MARS-approx substitutes consecutive minibatch gradients and the authors recommend it because observed degradation is marginal.

method.core_idea: Correct stochastic gradients recursively to reduce variance, then pass the correction through a chosen adaptive preconditioner.
method.mechanism: A scaled difference between gradients at adjacent parameters forms a STORM-like estimator; clipping and optimizer-specific first/second-moment or matrix statistics produce the update.
assumptions: Adjacent-minibatch gradient differences approximate the same-sample correction well enough in practice.
The selected clipping, learning-rate, and momentum schedules transfer across model scales.
GPT-2/OpenWebText performance is representative of broader foundation-model training.

techniques.role: Avoids the second same-sample backward pass by reusing adjacent-minibatch gradients.
Instantiates AdamW-, Lion-, and Shampoo-family variants in one framework.

evaluations.metric: Validation loss versus tokens and wall-clock time
evaluations.result: MARS variants converge faster across the reported scales; the 770M fixed-loss comparison is about 28B versus 50B tokens.
evaluations.baseline: AdamW, Lion, Muon, and Shampoo-family optimizers

evaluations.result: MARS-AdamW reports 44.64 compared with 41.70 for AdamW.
The approximation has marginal reported quality loss and avoids an extra gradient computation.

limitations: The largest experiment is a 770M GPT-2 model on one pretraining corpus.
MARS adds optimizer state and per-step arithmetic, and exact MARS needs an extra gradient evaluation.
Theory directly covers the exact estimator more cleanly than the recommended adjacent-minibatch approximation.
failure_modes: The recursive correction can become noisy when adjacent minibatches differ sharply.
Poor clipping or momentum settings can suppress useful gradient changes.
Token-efficiency gains may not offset implementation overhead on hardware or model families with different bottlenecks.
reusable_insights: Separate variance reduction from preconditioning so each component can be ablated and swapped.
Report both tokens-to-target and wall-clock-to-target for optimizer claims.
A practical approximation should be evaluated against the exact estimator, not only conventional baselines.
open_questions: Do MARS gains persist for modern multi-billion-parameter decoder, mixture-of-experts, and multimodal models?
Can the adjacent-batch approximation receive a convergence analysis under realistic data correlation?
Which curvature or gradient-noise measurements predict when each preconditioner wins?

competitive_landscape.title: Momentum-Based Variance Reduction in Non-Convex SGD
competitive_landscape.difference: STORM supplies the recursive same-sample correction; MARS scales and combines that mechanism with modern adaptive preconditioners for deep learning.

competitive_landscape.title: Adan: Adaptive Nesterov Momentum Algorithm for Faster Optimizing Deep Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Adan uses Nesterov-style gradient differences; MARS interprets a related update through variance reduction and exposes multiple preconditioners.

competitive_landscape.title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam
competitive_landscape.difference: SOAP stabilizes Shampoo by running Adam in an eigenbasis, whereas MARS first changes the stochastic gradient estimator and then permits matrix or diagonal preconditioning.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: recursive variance reduction and each preconditioner predate MARS. The contribution is a scaled unifying construction, an inexpensive adjacent-minibatch implementation, and controlled GPT-2 evidence across several optimizer families.
reviewer_notes: Full main text, experiments, ablations, derivations, and limitations were checked. Competitor primary records were checked 2026-08-23. Scale generalization remains untested beyond 770M parameters.
